summary.assessment: The run never invents data for a non-chart (all five diagrams and ECG traces declined with a one-line reason) and it transcribes printed numbers without a single error (B1 12 of 12, B3 15 of 15, C5 15 of 15); simple charts with a handful of marks per panel are also read well (C1 12 bars within 0.3 % of the axis, A3 and B4 within tolerance). It fails where many values must be located on the marks: box medians snap to whole numbers or tick values and the whiskers are lost (B5: 7 of 30 medians beyond 5 %, whisker ends null or collapsed to one value in 26 of 30 boxes), a dense line chart comes back as an unkeyed, miscounted sequence of the raw dots without the smoothed line (B2), and the stacked bars of C3 yield 58 numbers of which 45 exceed 100 % and none is a segment share. The vector path of C4, used without a model reading, is geometrically exact but structurally wrong: box outline vertices returned as a 'line' series under truncated labels, colour codes for series names, and the white-filled series dropped. Labels and metadata are weak even on correct figures (panel titles missing or scrambled in B3 and C5; the axis range taken from the tick labels that were read, so correct values beyond the last tick are flagged in B1 and C1), and its own checks expose C3 (61 issues, all confidences <= 0.55) but not C4's box panel (confidence 0.9) or B2, with no partial reading declared in `uncertain`. Trust it on figures with printed values, pies, and simple bar or interval charts; do not take its numbers from box plots, stacked or multi-series bars or dense line charts. The 11 usable figures are the 6 correct data charts plus the 5 true negatives, and the 4 OTHER codes are cosmetic label or metadata defects.
